taxonomic_note: Canonical genus corrected from source-pool Panicum obtusum to current Hopia obtusa. Panicum obtusum remains an important field-guide synonym.
look_here_first: VINE MESQUITE: FIRST trace a long creeping aboveground STOLON away from a leafy shoot; examine a swollen, densely hairy node where a new plant can root. THEN look at the narrow upright seedhead: short appressed raceme-like branches carry conspicuous smooth, rounded/oval blunt spikelets (not bermudagrass's radiating fingers). A tiny membranous ligule at the blade/sheath junction confirms a grass collar character but is not identified from the current photographs. Spikelets and root-bearing nodes must belong to the same plant.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Hopia obtusa and lists Texas in its native range; Panicum obtusum is a homotypic synonym. The project Hays County native source pool records the taxon under Panicum obtusum. The Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly records vine mesquite (Panicum obtusum) in Travis County. The Texas Hill Country grass treatment documents Hopia obtusa as a widespread Hill Country species; Blanco County is retained from the project's reviewed Hill Country source set.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

best_field_traits: WARM SEASON: native perennial forming patches/sod, sometimes found where runoff lingers; season and habitat are supporting clues only.
STOLONS: long slender tough aboveground runners can connect shoots; they are not simply loose roots.
ROOTING NODES: prominent swollen, often densely hairy/villous joints along stolons may root and produce new growth; photograph same connected runner.
SEEDHEAD: narrow upright panicle of 1–4 relatively short appressed raceme-like branches along central axis; may look like a single short spike from afar.
SPIKELETS: fairly large for this fine grass, blunt rounded oval, approximately 3–4 mm, generally smooth and without protruding awns; confirm with a scale and lens.
LEAVES: relatively flat to rolled blue-green blades, often 2–7 mm wide; size and glaucous color overlap with other grasses.
LIGULE: an actual membrane about 1–2 mm, not a fringe of hairs; do not infer it from fuzzy stolon nodes.
morphology_keys.joey_family_training: Poaceae family training: identify inflorescence architecture first, then inspect spikelets/glumes/lemma-palea/awns and ligule-collar-sheath characters.

comparisons.key_distinctions: BERMUDAGRASS (Cynodon dactylon) also creeps by stolons but usually has 3–7 slender DIGITATE one-sided fingers radiating near one point, rather than Hopia's narrow head of short appressed branches with stout blunt OVAL spikelets; its ligule is a short hair-fringed membranous rim. SWITCHGRASS (Panicum virgatum) normally forms taller erect clumps from rhizomes with a large open much-branched panicle, not vine mesquite's long aboveground node-rooting stolons. BUFFALOGRASS (Bouteloua dactyloides) is low sod-forming and dioecious, with contrasting separate male/female flowering structures rather than vine mesquite's oval spikelets. Do not identify from a vegetative patch or seedhead shape alone; trace the node and examine attached spikelets.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Terminal seedhead branching and a connected stolon node
field_matrix.this_species: Narrow inflorescence with short appressed branches and blunt oval spikelets; long hairy swollen rooting stolon nodes
field_matrix.look_alike: Several slender one-sided DIGITATE fingers from nearly one point; tiny hair-fringed ligule, creeping stolons
field_matrix.quick_rule: Runners alone do not decide; inspect the seedhead architecture and spikelet shape.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Entire rooted growth form and flowering head
field_matrix.this_species: Creeping aboveground stolon and slender narrow head of rounded blunt spikelets
field_matrix.look_alike: Erect rhizomatous bunch/sward with large open branching panicle, no Hopia-like long hairy stolon network
field_matrix.quick_rule: Narrow, appressed-branch seedhead plus rooting vine-like stolon favors Hopia.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Shoots plus flowering structures, male vs female
field_matrix.this_species: Usually higher flowering culms with narrow blunt-spikelet head
field_matrix.look_alike: Low sod with male flowers in comb-shaped branches and female flowers hidden in burs near foliage
field_matrix.quick_rule: Do not mistake any low turf runner for vine mesquite.

critical_photo_gaps: Same rooted Hopia plant photographed wide enough to trace one long aboveground stolon to a new rooted shoot; include a metric scale.
10–20× macro of an ACTUAL swollen hairy stolon node visibly emitting adventitious roots; do not arrow a nonrooting joint.
1-mm-scale inner MEMBRANOUS ligule at the leaf blade/sheath junction, with collar hairs separately visible if present.
10–20× side and face views of an intact attached ~3–4 mm rounded blunt spikelet showing glumes/veins; avoid claiming venation from distant seedheads.
Matched same-scale comparison: Hopia appressed branches and oval spikelets versus Cynodon digitately arranged thin one-sided fingers.
